title: ConfigBool silently fails on string values from CRD config
statement: ConfigBool uses v.(bool) type assertion which silently fails when CRD config stores values as YAML strings (e.g. "true"). Returns default false, causing silent misconfiguration.
evidence: Caused USE_CPU_OFFLOAD=0 despite config having cpuOffload: "true". Led to ROCm memory access fault crash-looping the sdxl-turbo-imagegen pod (12 restarts). Fixed in diffusers.go by switching to ConfigString, but ConfigBool itself is still broken for any future callers.
notes: ConfigBool workaround applied in diffusers.go only. ConfigBool in interface.go still has the bug. Any new backend using ConfigBool will hit the same silent failure. Fix: make ConfigBool handle string "true"/"false" values via strconv.ParseBool.

title: IfNotPresent pullPolicy causes stale image cache on tag reuse
statement: All control-plane and model deployments use pullPolicy: IfNotPresent with mutable tags (e.g. 'master', 'rocm-latest'). Node containerd caches old images by tag, requiring manual cache clearing or unique tags for every deploy.
evidence: Hit 3 times during this session: (1) proxy deployment after alias fix, (2) controller deployment after cpuOffload fix, (3) diffusers image update. Each required SSH into node + crictl rmi or unique SHA-tagged images to bypass cache.
notes: Options: (A) Use immutable SHA/commit tags in values.yaml and CI (eliminates cache issue). (B) Switch to pullPolicy: Always for mutable tags (adds registry dependency on every restart). (C) Use image digest pinning in values.yaml. Option A is cleanest — CI already tags images with CI_COMMIT_SHORT_SHA.

title: Diffusers image depends on unpinned base image and transitive deps
statement: rocm/pytorch:latest base image is unpinned. transformers, diffusers, and other Python deps float to latest, causing breaking import chains (MT5Tokenizer removal in transformers v5).
evidence: New diffusers build broke with 'cannot import name MT5Tokenizer from transformers' due to transformers v5.2.0 removing it. Required emergency pin to transformers>=4.40,<5 and adding sentencepiece dep.
notes: transformers pinned to <5 but rocm/pytorch base is still :latest. Should pin base image to a specific tag (e.g., rocm/pytorch:2.9.1-rocm7.1) and add a requirements.txt with pinned versions + hash verification.

title: Proxy model resolution only matched K8s resource name
statement: Proxy could not route requests by servedModelName or aliases — only by the K8s Model resource name. Users couldn't reach models through OpenWebUI/LiteLLM when using friendly names.
evidence: User couldn't chat with qwen3-30b-abliterated through OpenWebUI. HTTP requests to the proxy returned 404 for alias names. GitLab issue #12 created.
notes: Fixed with TTL-cached alias resolver (sync.Map + 5s refresh). 7 unit tests added. Deployed and verified.

title: Controller reconciliation produces no logs on deployment updates
statement: ensureDeployment() only logs on Create, not on Update. Makes it impossible to verify from logs whether the controller reconciled a model and what changes it applied.
evidence: During cpuOffload debugging, controller logs showed zero evidence of sdxl-turbo-imagegen reconciliation. Had to inspect ReplicaSet history and deployment env vars to determine if reconciliation occurred.
notes: Add structured log line at ensureDeployment update path: log.Info("Updating Deployment", "name", model.Name, "changedFields", diff). Consider using apiequality.Semantic.DeepEqual to detect actual changes before logging.

title: No fp16-fix VAE bundled for SDXL on ROCm
statement: SDXL models on ROCm require madebyollin/sdxl-vae-fp16-fix for artifact-free fp16 inference. Without it, fp32 is required (2x VRAM, slower). The VAE isn't bundled or cached.
evidence: RealVisXL V5.0 produced grainy images in fp16 due to VAE NaN artifacts. Had to fall back to fp32 as a workaround.
notes: Workaround: USE_FP16=0 (fp32). Proper fix: download madebyollin/sdxl-vae-fp16-fix to the SharedPVC cache, set VAE_PATH env var. This would allow fp16 with correct output (50% less VRAM, faster inference).

title: Docker and K3s containerd use separate image stores
statement: Images built and pushed via Docker on GPU nodes are not visible to K3s containerd. Requires separate pull or docker save | ctr import workflow.
evidence: docker save | k3s ctr images import required during diffusers image update. crictl pull sometimes resolves different manifests than docker push due to multi-arch manifest lists.
notes: Root cause: Docker Desktop on GPU nodes uses its own containerd, separate from K3s containerd. Options: (A) Build with buildctl/buildx pushing directly to Harbor, let K3s pull. (B) CI-only builds (no manual builds needed). (C) Use crane or skopeo to copy images between registries/stores.

title: GPU device misidentification: pod scheduled on iGPU instead of dGPU
statement: On cblevins-7900xtx (which has both iGPU and dGPU), some pod recreations land on the iGPU (AMD Radeon Graphics, 31GB shared) instead of the dGPU (Radeon RX 7900 XTX, 24GB).
evidence: During pod restarts, logs showed 'Device 0: AMD Radeon Graphics, Total memory: 31.0 GB' instead of 'Radeon RX 7900 XTX, 24.0 GB'. The k8s-device-plugin should isolate devices when amd.com/gpu is requested.
notes: Investigate AMD k8s-device-plugin configuration. The iGPU may need to be excluded from the device plugin's device list. Check /sys/class/drm/card*/device/vendor and renderD* device assignments.
